newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Nov inflation on track for euro goal.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Nov inflation on track for euro goal.

text.p: Portugal's average annual inflation in November, less favourable than expected, remains on track to meet the tough entry test for economic and monetary union, analysts said on Friday.
The determination of the Socialist government to keep the lid on inflation and to maintain a stable escudo are expected to ensure that the government keeps prices on a downward course, they said.
Portuguese average annual inflation, the government's yardstick, was 3.1 percent in November after 3.2 percent in October and 4.2 percent in November 1995.
"Average annual inflation is expected to meet the euro target," said Isabel Cabral, economist with Lisbon broker Fincor.
"I think Portugal has already hit the inflation target. The trend is what counts," said Rui Martins dos Santos, director of Banco Portugues de Investimento.
Nations opting to join EMU must have an annual inflation rate at the end of 1997 that is no more than 1.5 percent above the average of the EU's three best performers.
Six analysts contacted by Reuters had forecast a range of average annual inflation this year of between 3.0 and 3.2 percent and, at the end of 1997, between 2.4 and 3.0 percent.
Prices rose 0.2 percent in November, the National Statistics Institute said. Year-on-year inflation was 3.0 percent in November.
A poll of analysts contacted by Reuters had forecast that the price change in November would stand at between -0.2 and +0.1 percent.
"If Portugal aims to achieve the upper edge of its official limit, that is 2.5 percent, that should be enough to meet the euro target," said Cabral.
BPI's Martins dos Santos said: "According to the EU's own forecasts, Portugal would have to have an average annual inflation of below three percent to qualify for the euro."
